activities.title: Image in a shining spoon
activities.summary: View your face in the curved inner and outer surfaces of a spoon. Compare whether the image is smaller or larger and how it changes as you move the spoon.

activities.title: Sunlight focused by a convex lens
activities.summary: Hold a convex lens in sunlight and focus light on a sheet of paper. The bright spot is a real image of the Sun; concentrated heat can burn the paper.

activities.title: Real image of a candle on a screen
activities.summary: Use a concave mirror to form a sharp image of a candle flame on a screen. A screen is needed because the image is real.

activities.title: Tracing reflected rays from a plane mirror
activities.summary: Use pins and paper to locate incident and reflected rays for a plane mirror and verify the laws of reflection.

activities.title: Image formation by a concave mirror
activities.summary: Observe how object position affects image size and nature for a concave mirror (near F, at C, beyond C).

activities.title: Image formation by a convex mirror
activities.summary: Form always erect, diminished, virtual images with a convex mirror regardless of object distance.

activities.title: Refraction through a rectangular glass slab
activities.summary: Trace light through a glass slab; emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced.

activities.title: Refraction through water in a beaker
activities.summary: A coin at the bottom of a beaker appears raised because light bends away from the normal on leaving water.

activities.title: Bending of a pencil in water
activities.summary: Part of a pencil in water looks displaced at the surface due to refraction at the air–water boundary.

activities.title: Image by a convex lens on a screen
activities.summary: Focus sunlight or a distant object with a convex lens to obtain a real, inverted image on a screen.

activities.title: Lens lines and focal points on a table
activities.summary: Mark F and 2F on a table; place object beyond 2F and locate the real image formed by a convex lens.

activities.title: Virtual image with a concave lens
activities.summary: View an object through a concave (diverging) lens — image is erect, virtual, and diminished.

activities.title: Power of a lens
activities.summary: Compare lenses of different focal lengths; shorter focal length means greater converging power (higher dioptre).

exercise_mcqs.question: Which one of the following materials cannot be used to make a lens?
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Clay is opaque and cannot form a transparent lens.

exercise_mcqs.question: The image formed by a concave mirror is observed to be virtual, erect and larger than the object. Where should be the position of the object?
options: Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
Between the pole of the mirror and its principal focus
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Virtual, erect, enlarged images from a concave mirror occur when the object is between P and F.

exercise_mcqs.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real image of the size of the object?
options: At the principal focus of the lens
Between the optical centre of the lens and its principal focus
exercise_mcqs.explanation: At u = 2f, a convex lens forms a real image of the same size at v = 2f.

exercise_mcqs.question: A spherical mirror and a thin spherical lens have each a focal length of –15 cm. The mirror and the lens are likely to be
options: the mirror is concave and the lens is convex
the mirror is convex, but the lens is concave
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Negative focal length (New Cartesian sign convention) indicates a concave mirror and a concave (diverging) lens.

exercise_mcqs.question: No matter how far you stand from a mirror, your image appears erect. The mirror is likely to be
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Plane and convex mirrors always give erect images; concave mirrors can give inverted real images.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which of the following lenses would you prefer to use while reading small letters found in a dictionary?
options: A convex lens of focal length 50 cm
A concave lens of focal length 50 cm
A convex lens of focal length 5 cm
A concave lens of focal length 5 cm
exercise_mcqs.explanation: A convex lens is a magnifier; shorter focal length gives greater magnification for nearby objects.

intext_samples.question: In the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, which sign convention is used for distances measured against the direction of incident light?
intext_samples.explanation: Distances measured against the direction of incident light are negative in the NCERT sign convention.

intext_samples.question: Refractive index n = c/v compares the speed of light in vacuum to that in the medium. If light slows down in glass, n is
intext_samples.explanation: When v < c, the ratio c/v exceeds 1.
